subject: RFI: Key Custody, BYO-Import and Attestation for Enterprise Deployment
messages:
From: Elena Ramos <elena.ramos@stratagem.com>
To: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwood.com>
Cc: Stratagem Security <security@stratagem.com>
Date: Sat, 29 Aug 2026 11:12:00 -0700
Subject: RFI: Key custody and BYO-import operational details

Ava / Redwood team,

Thanks for taking this. As part of our vendor selection for the inference layer, our security and procurement teams have a few detailed questions about your key management approach. Please see the attached RFI and confirm whether Redwood can provide the following or describe how you handle these scenarios: 

- BYO key import into your HSM-backed KMS (import formats supported, dual-control process, split knowledge, safeguards during import)
- Whether Redwood operates key escrow for customer keys; if so, what controls and legal constructs (escrow agreements) are used
- Attestation options (on-demand signed attestation of key custody & HSM configuration)
- Rotation windows for root/master keys vs. data-encryption keys and recommended frequency
- TLS and mutual-TLS support for control-plane connections (cipher suites, minimum TLS version)
- Audit log evidence (KV of key usage, admin actions) and how long logs are retained

We'd like a written response for the RFP (native PDF) plus any supporting evidence (FIPS certs, attestation template). Can you also describe the operational steps for an import test (we'll want to do a test import and verify key usage end-to-end)?

Target timeline: initial answers by end of next week, attestation/attachments in two weeks.

Thanks,
Elena Ramos
Senior InfoSec Manager
Stratagem Analytics

Attachment: RFI_KeyMgmt_Strategem.pdf (application/pdf, 412KB) 
From: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwood.com>
To: Elena Ramos <elena.ramos@stratagem.com>
Cc: Stratagem Security <security@stratagem.com>
Date: Tue, 01 Sep 2026 09:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: RFI: Key custody and BYO-import operational details

Elena —

Appreciate the clear list. High-level answers below; I attached a concise operational FAQ and our BYO import runbook for the test. If helpful, we can schedule a 30-minute deep-dive.

1) BYO import and dual-control
- Supported import formats: PKCS#8 (PEM/DER), PKCS#12.
- Imports are performed into FIPS 140-2/3 Level 3 HSM partitions (Thales/Utimaco-backed HSMs in our Dedicated and Private deployments).
- Dual-control: imports require two distinct operator steps (split knowledge). One operator initiates and uploads encrypted key material; a second operator completes activation. All operator identities are authenticated via SSO + MFA and logged.
- Secure transport: import over mutually authenticated TLS (mTLS) channel using ephemeral session certs; we never accept plaintext key material over public channels.

2) Key escrow and custody
- Default: Redwood does NOT escrow customer private keys. Customers retain sole ownership; we store keys in customer-dedicated HSM partitions.
- Escrow option: available by exception under an MSA addendum (e.g., for disaster recovery in certain regulated workflows). Escrow keys are stored encrypted under a split-key scheme and require a notarized release process plus an execution of an escrow agreement.

3) Attestations and evidence
- We provide signed attestation letters for HSM configuration, FIPS module IDs, and import processes. Attestations are signed by Redwood Security leadership and can be timeboxed (for a specific date).
- Formal evidence package includes: HSM FIPS certificates, KMS audit log extracts for a defined window, and a procedural import checklist.

4) Rotation policy
- Root/KEK (Key-Encrypting Keys): rotation recommended every 12 months; supported immediate rotation on request.
- Data encryption keys (DEKs): recommended rotation 90 days for higher-sensitivity workloads; 180 days typical for general workloads. Rotation is performed with automatic re-encryption/rolling via the runtime; we offer hot-swap rotation with minimal disruption.

5) TLS / mutual TLS
- Control plane: TLS 1.3 preferred; TLS 1.2 allowed with modern ciphers. We support ECDHE_AESGCM and CHACHA20_POLY1305 suites.
- mTLS: supported for inbound customer-managed control-plane connections and for BYO import sessions.

6) Audit logs and retention
- Admin and key-usage events are logged with immutable write-once backends. Default retention: 13 months. Longer retention available as an enterprise add-on. Logs include operator identity, IP, operation type (import, rotate, usage), and object id.

Operational test (short runbook excerpt)
- Step 1: Customer generates key pair in their environment (or we can generate via a customer HSM).
- Step 2: Customer exports key in PKCS#8 and encrypts it with a temporary site-wrapped key.
- Step 3: Customer uploads to Redwood over mTLS to a signed import session.
- Step 4: Two operators in sequence complete the import; system issues confirmation and transaction id.
- Step 5: Customer performs a test signing/encryption call; we provide audit log snippet for the transaction id.

Attachments: redwood-kms-byo-operations.pdf (runbook), sample-cli-commands.txt

If you want the full MSA escrow language for review, I can loop in Legal.

Cheers,
Ava Chen
Senior Solutions Engineer — Redwood Inference
ava.chen@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0192
